title: Neighbourhood presentation of the strict-local derived mate
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ a geometric point, $g:S_{(s)}\to S$ its strict-henselization map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], $X'=X\times_S S_{(s)}$, $p:X'\to X$, and $f':X'\to S_{(s)}$. For every $K\in D^+(\operatorname{Ab}(X_{et}))$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, the map $m=\Gamma(S_{(s)},H^n(\mathrm{mate}_K))$ has a global cohomology continuity presentation with base $T=X$, object $K$, and degree $n$ [def-weil-pbc-global-cohomology-continuity-presentation]. The source cocone is colimiting and the composite of each source leg with $m$ is the canonical projection pullback. No target colimit or invertibility assertion is made.

source.place: Tags 03Q9 (theorem-higher-direct-images), 03Q8 and 0GIT; presentation of neighbourhood restriction maps

proof.text: Choose the original small-colimit neighbourhood geometry with smallModel_nonempty_strictLocalNeighbourhoodGeometry, and its projection identifications with smallModel_nonempty_strictLocalMateProjectionData. The domain diagram and source legs are the explicit derived-sections presheaf and germ map. The canonical strictLocalization implementations are a different model and are not imported.

Apply smallModel_isColimit_strictLocalCohomologySourceLegs to the derived direct image. Assemble every field of GlobalCohomologyContinuityPresentation using this source colimit, the original geometry, the projection equations and the exact strict-local Leray target isomorphism. No continuity or invertibility theorem is used.

Use the general pointed-section-cone restriction on strictLocalSectionCone, the existing exact-sections instance for the small colimit model, and the general exact-global-sections Leray comparison wherever the former specialized restriction API was used. The cone restriction has the same section formulas, its germ predicate is definitionally identical, and uniqueness identifies the chosen stalk maps. All other argument steps and all scheme models stay as before.
